name: Ransomware Locks Case Management
description: Ransomware encrypts the case management system across the district; hearings proceed from paper files while clerks rebuild dockets.
assumptions: Hearings continue on paper; the loss is docket reconstruction and delay administration.
Secondary loss covers speedy-trial and statutory-deadline consequences.

name: Sealed and Expunged Records Exposure
description: An intrusion exposes sealed case files, juvenile records, and expunged matters — the records the court is most strictly obligated to protect.
assumptions: Protected-party safety (protective orders, juveniles) drives the high-end estimates.
Primary loss covers investigation, notification, and protective measures.
Secondary loss covers civil liability and legislative or supreme-court oversight.

name: E-Filing Platform Outage
description: Attacks on the e-filing portal block filings near statutory deadlines, forcing emergency deadline orders and paper fallback.
assumptions: Standing administrative orders toll deadlines during declared outages.
Primary loss covers restoration, clerk overtime, and emergency communications.
Secondary loss covers disputes over prejudiced filings despite tolling orders.

name: Juror Information Breach
description: The jury management system is breached, exposing juror questionnaires with home addresses and employment details across trial pools.
assumptions: High-profile trial pools raise both attacker interest and consequence severity.
Primary loss covers notification, juror support, and pool re-qualification.
Secondary loss covers mistrial motions and juror-safety measures in active trials.

name: Fines and Fees Payment System Fraud
description: Attackers compromise the online fines-and-fees payment flow, skimming cards and redirecting settlement batches from the payment processor.
asset: Court payment portal and remittance flows
assumptions: The processor bears card losses; the court's loss is response, reconciliation, and refunds.
Primary loss covers forensics and payer notification.
Secondary loss covers restitution-tracking corrections and state auditor findings.
